module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 31

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/31](https://www.erdosproblems.com/31)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er59] Erdős, P., *Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Sammelband zu Ehren des 250.
  Geburtstages Leonhard Eulers (1959), 116-119.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial
  theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
- [Lo54] Lorentz, G. G., *On a problem of additive number theory*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1954), 838-841.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos31

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

/--
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos31.lean"]
theorem erdos_31 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite →
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B := by
  sorry

end Erdos31

reformulations.difference: The original cited papers phrase A and B as increasing infinite sequences. Lean uses an infinite set A and allows the density-zero witness B to be finite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every infinite subset of ℕ has a strictly increasing enumeration. Conversely, if the Lean witness B is finite (or merely not known to be infinite), replace it by B ∪ {k² : k ∈ ℕ}. This union is infinite and still has natural density zero, since both constituent sets have density zero. Enlarging B preserves eventual coverage by A+B. Thus requiring an infinite sequence B does not change the existence claim.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Problems and results in additive number theory (1956), §4, p. 132: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1956-17.pdf
P. Erdős, Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie (1959), §3, p. 117: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1959-27.pdf

review.notes: Checked the file’s sole declaration and its density, cardinality, sumset, and filter semantics. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, review_statement_iff proves equivalence with ordinary real-valued natural density zero and finiteness of the unrepresentable natural numbers; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary tests also pass: counting intervals are finite, the denominator at n=0 is harmless, empty A is excluded, and empty B cannot satisfy coverage. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/31 and the Lorentz paper was blocked; the four cited Erdős papers establish the intended claim and Lorentz attribution. The current community database agrees with the recorded solved/Lean status. The linked proof has an equivalent statement and no explicit sorry or custom axioms; its original v4.29.1 build was not reproduced, and attempting it with the supplied v4.33.1 environment encountered compatibility errors.
